- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes in history.
- Underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, suggesting lag or failure to capture near-term downward pressure.
- Overreacts to recent high values (overshoots after spikes), then fails to correct downward quickly.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated — model holds too much upward bias after peaks, ignoring historical tendency to revert.
- Forecasts for 30-day horizon show persistent bias toward lower values, especially when history includes strong downward trends.
- Model tends to underestimate volatility in the final 10 days, leading to overly optimistic price trajectories.
- When history shows a clear downward trend, model often fails to adjust forecast downward early enough — lagging correction.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to capture short-term volatility or sudden reversals in price direction.
